takeaways: Profit beat, revenue missed: $4.66 of adjusted EPS vs $4.49 expected, but reported revenue of $8.89 billion fell short of the $9.55 billion forecast (FactSet via Dow Jones).

The revenue miss is mostly a one-time item: Booking booked a $900 million revenue reduction tied to a Federal Trade Commission matter. Excluding it, "adjusted revenue" was $9.8 billion, up 9%, per the release.
The actual business grew: gross bookings (the total value of trips booked) rose 10% to $54.5 billion and room nights rose 7% to 345 million, both ahead of estimates (Dow Jones).

The worry is the outlook. Booking expects only 1-3% room-night growth and 2-4% gross bookings growth in Q4, saying travel demand cooled late in the quarter, with Middle East disruption, higher fuel costs and airfares, and unrest in some European cities weighing on October (Dow Jones).
It kept its full-year outlook for gross bookings and adjusted EPS (Dow Jones). Note: the share price is lower than you may remember because of the 25-for-1 stock split in April.
verdict: Booking beat on profit, missed on revenue thanks to a $900 million FTC hit, and then said Q4 travel is slowing to a stroll. The stock dipped after hours because investors buy the next quarter, not the last one. Good trip, bumpy landing.
